name: Abihu
overview: Abihu was a male member of the tribe of Levi and the son of Aaron. He is notably remembered for his death as a result of offering strange fire to the LORD, an act that was forbidden. This incident highlights his unique role and tragic end within the priestly lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Abihu means 'he is [my] father,' reflecting a personal or familial significance. This proper name is recorded in Exodus 6:23 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Abihu was the son of Aaron and Elisheba, as indicated in Exodus 6:23 and Numbers 26:60. Scripture records these familial ties but does not mention other relationships beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Abihu's significance in Scripture centers on his role as a priestly son of Aaron who died for disobedience in worship by offering unauthorized fire to the LORD. His story serves as a sobering reminder of the holiness required in approaching God and the serious consequences of disregarding His commands. This event underscores the importance of reverence and obedience in service to God within the Levitical priesthood.
